newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan money rates end up on borrowing pressure.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan money rates end up on borrowing pressure.

text.p: Pakistan's money market rates closed higher on Monday on borrowing pressure but may plunge on Tuesday owing to an inflow of about 4.5 billion rupees on the maturity of paper sold in an open market operation, dealers said.

The overnight deals were struck in the range of 11 and 13 percent early in the day, but they moved up to 14 percent amid borrowing pressure and some deals were done at 18 percent at the end of the day, a dealer at Standard Chartered Bank said.
He said the State (central) Bank of Pakistan (SBP) received bids worth 6.8 billion rupees in an auction of six-month short-term federal bonds, whose result would be announced on Tuesday.
The inflow of 4.5 billion rupees is likely to keep the overnight rates depressed on Tuesday even if the SBP does not conduct a special open market operation on the day, dealers said.
